children: , the pharmaceutical and medical-technology powerhouse, rose roughly 1% to $277.955 Thursday afternoon. Investors barely flinched after AbbVie's experimental multiple-myeloma drug, etentamig, produced a 74% response rate and lowered the risk of disease progression or death by 60% versus standard therapies.

AbbVie's trial announcement puts a convenient monthly treatment into the myeloma race, with potential use in outpatient settings. But J&J is defending a fast-growing franchise: its second-quarter results identified Carvykti as a major engine behind 6.8% operational growth in Innovative Medicine.

Here is the crucial point: Reuters said etentamig currently looks most differentiated after CAR-T therapy, not as an immediate Carvykti substitute. The market is treating AbbVie's success as category expansion, not a direct hit to J&J. Still, expectations are already stretchedthe $277.955 share price stands 44.08% above J&J's $192.92 GF Value estimate, making future safety and durability data impossible to ignore.

title: J&J Gains as AbbVie Posts 74% Myeloma Response
